title: The Unfriend by Steven Moffat, dir. Mark Gatiss, with Reece Shearsmith - review & photos
transcript: hello and welcome to one minute theater reviews i'm paul seven lewis this is the minerva at chichester and i'm here to see the unfriend what connects doctor who sherlock the league of gentlemen and inside number nine answers on a postcard please not really i'm going to tell you it's the unfriend a laugh-a-minute comedy that's just opened at chichester festival theatre's minerva studio and i'll give you all those connections in a moment but for now let's just say that stephen moffat writer and showrunner for doctor who and creator of sherlock has finally got around to writing a stage play at the age of 60. and that's encouraging for we older folk to think it's never too late but i doubt there are many playwrights of any age who can make such a triumphant debut the man has comedy bones and the laughs come thick and fast he knows how to make old jokes sound fresh he understands how to give the actors the opportunity to use their faces and their bodies and what actors francis barber is a loud confident american who turns out to be a serial murderer uh rhys shear smith and amanda rabington are the couple she befriends and who then can't get rid of her because they're too polite and although much of the praise should go to francis barbara's bravura performance i did love richard smith's comic timing and his panic-stricken face it's a long time since i laughed so much well that's the one minute review but please keep watching because i have a lot more to tell you about this wonderful comedy first the connections stephen moffat who wrote the young friend is best known probably for doctor who which he co-wrote during the first decade to serve its new incarnation he also created benedict cumberbatch's sherlock which he co-wrote with mark gattis who's the director of the unfriend and we know him from the league of gentlemen which also starred richard smith who co-writes inside number nine and stars in the unfriend which also stars amanda rabington who was watson's wife in sherlock and francis barber who played madame cavarian in doctor who when stephen muffet was the showrunner so they know one another they work well together the basic premise is that an overbearing american woman called elsa meets peter and debbie an english couple on a cruise and invites herself to their house they're too polite to say no you get a glimpse of their front door which has the number nine on it a little in joke maybe but it's a hint that we shouldn't be surprised when it turns out she's no simple pain in the neck let's soon discover she's a serial murderer but they're still too polite to chuck her out this is a comedy of manners literally i suspect how much you like it may depend on how much you identify with the self-defeating politeness and embarrassment of our suburban english couple if you're happy to complain about the service in a restaurant talk to your doctor about intimate infections or barter with sales people well you may well find this plot unbelievable you might also refuse to suspend your disbelief because the characters seem too much like stereotypes the over lovely polite brits who won't say what they're thinking the loud brash american who makes jokes about a woman who's obese but the thing is people who are non-confrontational and those who are blunt to the point of rudeness are actually found throughout the world but more than that stephen moffat subverts each stereotype peter is actually quite rude even if he doesn't express it verbally for example he ignores his neighbor even when he's in the room talking to him and our caller spade a bloody shovel american may be a killer but she has a positive effect on this dysfunctional family the previously grunting son and negative daughter two more stereotypes who turn out to have depth a beauty and are beautifully played by gabriel howell and maddie holliday become happy chatty loving kids she's murder popping says debbie by the way the neighbor is a classic boar but he too serves a more subtle function because he reminds us of the claustrophobia of suburban life with its low level passive aggressive as elsa says rankling over boundary walls and parking spaces and it helps us understand why residents of estates might need to be overly polite just to prevent all hell breaking loose the neighbor is played to droning but sly perfection by michael simpkins we do meet a police officer who's not a stereotype oh he's not in the sense of the hard cops you so often see in tv dramas he's another character subject to shyness and embarrassment and given a scene stealing performance by marcus honolulu although it's his theatrical debut stephen moffat hits the boards running his understanding of the stage is impressive the unfriend has structure varying pace and flowing comedy i mean you know how in comedy sometimes the jokes or the situation or particular characters can seem forced not here the jokes flow naturally for example russia smith's character is so tight someone says he would sever a proctologist's finger at the joint in fact mr moffatt doesn't force anything he gives room for rishir smith to contort his face with surprise or embarrassment or amanda rabington to express per slipped annoyance i assume a lot of credit should go to director mark gattis for the comic timing and the exemplary way the stage is used by the actors the set by robert jones is a triumph i mean it can't be easy to create a suburban middle class home when you have an audience on three sides but with wooden flooring a staircase an l-shaped sofa and see-through areas at the back for kitchen and lobby combined with the projection of the exterior of the house mr jones does just that in the second act we continue on tender hooks about whether elsa will poison the game but the funniest scene in the play is triggered by the fact that peter's embarrassment inevitably extends to talking about toilet matters see i'm embarrassed already so there's an extended scene involving him trying to find a reason to examine the um poo of someone in the toilet in case they've been poisoned and of course our embarrassment as an audience is almost as acute as his if you do go to see the unfriend and i recommend that you do you might be anticipating the punchline long before it arrives but you're still likely to be applauding when it does i give the unfriend five stars i hope you enjoyed this review or at least found it useful and if you did why not subscribe and you'll be the first to know about my future reviews you can read my
